rv.q: And, in a strangely exciting way, it mostly holds up.
Despite the raw banter and the actors' solid performances (especially Abbott), "Danny and the Deep Blue Sea" isn't exactly riveting.
Certainly, it adds to the raw beauty and poignancy of Mr. Shanley’s short and enduringly bittersweet play.
Danny and the Deep Blue Sea may be a small play but it has a big heart beating erratically beneath its turbulent surface.
Abbott excellently teases out Danny's tender side, finding the various shades of the character.
Abbott and Plaza make a radiant, inevitable pairing; both having outgrown their roots in indelible, early Millennial series into appealingly complex careers.
Shanley's writing is lyrical enough that this solid revival casts a spell anyway, but one may also leave the theater wondering about the more devastating experience that it might have been.
It’s evocative, alluring design, but excess window dressing for a small display.

The latest to attempt the feat are Christopher Abbott and Aubrey Plaza, who lead an already-sold-out run at Off Broadway's tiny Lucille Lortel Theatre that demonstrates both the appeal of Shanley's 1983 drama as well as some of its shortcomings.

cn.t: Plaza and Abbott deliver knockout performances in Shanley's intense two-hander, though critics are divided on whether the 1983 play's operatic brutality and profanity-packed romance still resonates or simply feels dated and disturbing.

vr.q: I wouldn't be able to justify the triple digit ticket price that a lot of people are paying to see them in this otherwise average play.
